# C — Remove the discovery-step friction for Serena's symbol tools (config only)

## Context / Problem

The mechanism most directly responsible for the observed failure was **friction asymmetry**, not missing
guidance. In the session that prompted this epic, `Bash` was already loaded and in active use for `rebar` and
`pytest`, while Serena's symbol tools were **deferred** — their schemas were not loaded, so using them required
an extra `ToolSearch` round-trip first. `grep` cost zero extra steps. Under that gradient the cheaper tool wins
whatever the documentation says.

## Verified ground truth (probed 2026-07-29; supersedes the original plan's assumptions)

The original plan assumed a per-tool "mark these tools non-deferred" lever and a repo-local config file to put it
in. Both assumptions were wrong. What is actually true:

1. **Deferral is all-or-nothing.** The only control is the env var `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`
   (`true` | `false` | `auto` | `auto:N`, where `auto:N` defers once combined tool definitions exceed N% of the
   context window). It is settable from `.claude/settings.json`'s `env` block. There is **no per-MCP-server and
   no per-tool** non-deferral setting — so "limit the always-loaded set to <= 4 Serena navigation tools" is
   **not implementable**, and this story's AC is corrected below accordingly.
   (Ref: `code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/tool-search` → "Configure tool search".)
2. **`AGENTS.md:173` is inaccurate.** It states "Serena's tools load at session start". The *server* connects at
   session start; its *tool schemas* do not. Directly observed: in a Claude Code session in this repo,
   `mcp__serena__find_symbol`, `find_referencing_symbols` and `get_symbols_overview` were all listed as deferred
   and required a `ToolSearch` call before use. This confirms the friction the epic diagnoses is real, and the
   false claim in `AGENTS.md` is corrected by story `1ecf-fe38-9247-421b` (D), which owns that file.
3. **`.claude/` is git-ignored** (`.gitignore:38`), so a repo-committed setting needs an un-ignore negation.
4. **Settings resolve to the main checkout**, shared by all worktrees — there is no per-worktree project
   settings file. So a change landed here takes effect in the operator's next session in the repo, not in the
   worktree session that authored it.

## Approach

Ship a **repo-committed** `.claude/settings.json` that sets the one lever that exists, plus the `.gitignore`
negation that lets exactly that file be tracked (`.claude/` stays ignored otherwise, so operator-local
`settings.local.json`, `scratch/` and `worktrees/` are unaffected).

**The tradeoff is now global, so state it honestly and measure it.** Because the lever is all-or-nothing,
turning deferral off loads *every* connected server's schemas up front, not just Serena's three. That cost scales
with whatever MCP servers the operator has connected, which the repo cannot control. So: measure the actual
input-token delta on a trivial headless run with the setting on vs off, record the number on this ticket, and
choose between `"false"` (never defer) and `"auto:N"` (defer only past an N% budget) on that evidence rather
than on assumption. Prefer the smallest setting that keeps Serena's tools resident.

Reverting is deleting one key from one JSON file; there is no code path to unwind.

## Scope

- `.claude/settings.json` — new, tracked: the `env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` setting (and nothing else that changes
  agent behaviour).
- `.gitignore` — negation so `.claude/settings.json` alone is tracked.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — a short note: what the setting does, the measured cost, and the one-line revert.

## Testing

- A test asserts the tracked `.claude/settings.json` is valid JSON and sets `env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` to one of
  the documented values (guards against a typo silently disabling the whole point).
- A test asserts `.claude/settings.json` is **tracked** by git while `.claude/` remains ignored (i.e. the
  negation works and did not un-ignore `settings.local.json`).
- Empirical: a headless `claude -p` run measures the input-token delta with the setting on vs off; the numbers
  are recorded on this ticket. (A fresh *interactive* transcript showing `find_referencing_symbols` invoked with
  no preceding `ToolSearch` is only observable after the change lands in the operator's checkout, so it is
  recorded as a post-land confirmation, not a pre-land gate.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a tracked `.claude/settings.json` sets `env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` such that MCP tool schemas — Serena's
      included — are not deferred, and a test pins that the file is valid JSON with a documented value
- [ ] `.gitignore` tracks exactly `.claude/settings.json` and still ignores the rest of `.claude/` (proven by a
      test, so `settings.local.json` can never be swept in)
- [ ] the story records WHY the always-loaded set could not be limited to the <= 4 named Serena tools (no
      per-tool lever exists) — the corrected finding, not silent under-delivery
- [ ] the measured input-token cost of the setting is recorded on this ticket, and the chosen value is justified
      against that measurement
- [ ] the change is configuration only, with a one-line revert documented in `docs/`
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass
